exposure: Use of medicinal plants during labor and delivery (e.g., Lepidium sativum L., Crocus sativus L., Cinnamomum verum J. Presl., Peganum harmala L.)
cohort: The cohort consists of 216 women who used medicinal plants during labor and delivery, identified from 22,523 delivery records at the regional hospital of Guelmim, Morocco, between 2015 and 2021.
finding: The use of medicinal plants during labor was frequently associated with adverse maternal and fetal complications, including fetal/neonatal distress and post-partum hemorrhage, although it also correlated with a significant reduction in labor duration.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery, which occurred in 65% of cases among women using medicinal plants, was associated with a significant reduction in the duration of labor.
